Distribution Surface — Proof Set

S5/S6 · drawn 2026-08-15 · logical pixels · ResponsiveLayout.DENSITY_TOKENS · unpainted (UUI-16)

One skeleton — holder · pool · detail — rendered for eight consumers at four viewports, to test whether convoy, loadout, skills, styles, battalions, shop, forge and on-map Trade are one surface with adapters or several surfaces that merely rhyme.

The hypothesis under test. LDC-1 already rules one mechanism for every cap-bound category (earned superset → equipped subset → cap). RPD-11 rules Manage Roster an open registry of panels. EPUX-24 rules one atomic quote/commit core with shop and forge as thin panels over it. BAT-10 and CNV-8 both delegate presentation to "the existing equip/loadout affordances", which have never been drawn. If those rulings are right, one skeleton should serve all eight. These frames are where that either holds or visibly fails.

Status: hypotheses. Nothing here is an accepted UI contract. Frames drawn against a ruling carry the id in a solid chip; frames drawn against a recommendation or an open proposal carry a dashed chip. Measurements are read from the rendered layout, not estimated.

1 · One skeleton, eight consumers — Expanded (1920×1080)

The reference composition. Every frame below is the same three columns — holder, pool, detail — with the same chrome: one app-bar line and one control row. Only the adapter changes. If the skeleton is real, these frames should be boring, and the differences between a convoy and a battalion roster should be entirely in the data.

2 · The Compact floor (360×640) — the chain

At the design floor the three regions become three steps. The control band takes 45% of the display (UUI-3), leaving a 352-px canvas; the chrome is one app bar plus one control row. These frames measure what is left for content, and whether the detail column — which must carry the consequence before the verb — fits it.

3 · On-map (852×393) — the tightest surface in the program

The 4:3 game rect at this viewport is 524 logical px — the number UUI-19 and the shop album hit independently. Battlefield shop, Trade and provider convoy all render here. The proposal drawn: an on-map distribution surface takes the canvas region only and never the control band, inheriting the conversation ruling from DRC.

5 · The dependent-choice layer — one pick, then a set that only exists because of it

Owner proposal, 2026-08-15. Trade picks an item and then a counterpart in someone else's inventory; the forge picks an item and then a modification to apply to it. Drawn here as one layer with two kinds of second set — counterpart (another instance, which will be displaced or swapped) and operation (a transform applied to the first pick) — and a third consumer, replacing a skill at a full cap, to test whether the layer generalizes past the two surfaces that prompted it.

The constraint it is drawn against. EPUX-26 rejected a second navigation level for the forge (item → mode → operation) because EPUX-03 caps the chain at two adjacent panes. So the dependent set replaces a region and never adds a fourth. Two placements are drawn — P, the set takes the pool region, and D, the set takes the detail region, which is EPUX-26's ruled shape for the forge — so the measurement can decide rather than taste.

The gesture is already ratified. RPD's auto-fill-then-swap placement model is select-then-select, committing on the second selection, with no confirm because a swap is reversible and so earns no CAU-4 tag. This layer is that gesture's fourth consumer, not a new one.

4 · The Expanded boundary (1024×768)

Three columns at their narrowest. This is where a shared skeleton either holds or has to collapse to two panes — and the answer must be the same for every consumer, or the family fragments.
